Approve, narrowly as a reversible rate-gate/pacing A/B. The gate can reject a render call solely on `T0 + Interval/2 < NextAt`; your numbers are consistent with about one such rejection per second (`59.5–59.6 − ~1 ≈ 58.5–58.6`), but do not prove that is the only loss.

Add a 10 s warm-up after each cap change and repeat the 60 baseline after 61—and after 62, if used. Run 62 only if 61 is clean but still below target. Keep your 120 s windows, UTC/receipt logging, unique-director-fps and ≤0.5% drop criteria, and six-core CPU limit. From existing samplers, compare `Captured`, `RateSkipped`, `DroppedSlots`, `DupCalls`/`MissedFrames`, accepted-versus-unique/received/written counts, queue-drop deltas, and encode/copy/queue latency. Stop early on sustained queue growth, increased slot/queue drops, or CPU budget breach.

Restore 60 afterward unless deliberately retaining the winning cap for a separate soak. Cap headroom can diagnose gate sensitivity; it does not establish queue/delivery capacity. Also, 19.9 ms encoding exceeds the 16.67 ms frame period: serial encoding cannot sustain 60, so overlap and queue behavior require separate measurement.
